instructions: Boil a kettle of water. Remove the stems and seeds from the guajillo and ancho chiles and tear them into pieces. Put them in a heatproof bowl, cover with the boiling water and leave them for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the pork into 1-inch pieces and pat them dry. Toss them with 1 tsp salt, the black pepper and 1/2 tsp of the cumin.
Cut the onion in half. Add a quarter of the onion to a blender with the garlic. Dice the rest of the onion.

Heat the oil in a large wide pot over medium-high heat. Add the pork in two batches and cook each for 3 minutes, turning once, until browned. Transfer the first batch to a plate while the second cooks, then return all of it to the pot.
Drain the soaked chiles and add them to the blender with 1 cup of the broth, the remaining 1/2 tsp cumin and 1/2 tsp salt. Blend for 1 minute, until smooth.

Add the diced onion to the pork and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the chile sauce and the remaining 1 cup of broth. Bring to a simmer, then turn the heat to medium-low and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Drain and rinse the nopales. Stir them in and cook for 5 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a piece. No thermometer? Cut one open: it should be white or faintly blush, with clear juices.
Serve with the warm corn tortillas.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: The lead is In Mama Maggie's Kitchen's red chile (guajillo and ancho blended with broth, pork browned first, nopales added at the end), cross-checked against Maricruz Avalos, who uses jarred nopales and a lighter chile sauce. Both simmer pork in the sauce for a long time; this uses boneless pork loin in 1-inch pieces so it is tender in 15 minutes, and jarred nopales so there is no boiling step. Broth is gluten-free. In Mama Maggie's has only 11 ratings, so this is a fallback lead.
